summary: Encore by Mingara on the NSW Central Coast is a five-storey, 86-room hotel designed by Marchese Partners. This Project Spotlight explores the architectural intent, bathroom specification strategy, and the role of cohesive ceramic solutions in delivering long-term hospitality performance.
title: Encore By Mingara — Marchese Partners
bodyHtml:
Encore by Mingara — a contemporary hotel environment defined by clarity of form and material consistency.

Encore by Mingara — Marchese Partners

Encore by Mingara, located at Tumbi Umbi on the NSW Central Coast, is a five-storey, 86-room hotel designed to complement and support the existing Mingara Recreation Club precinct. Completed in 2025, the project was recently recognised at the 2025 Newcastle Excellence in Building Awards.

Engaged by Mingara Leisure Group, Marchese Partners led the architectural and interior design for Encore by Mingara, shaping an environment defined by generous, homely guest rooms and a relaxed coastal sensibility. The design approach prioritised clarity of form, material consistency, and durability — resolving the hotel as a refined, contemporary environment suited to the demands of long-term hospitality use.

Within the bathrooms, this thinking was carried through into a restrained specification approach, with ceramic elements, fittings, and finishes selected as part of a cohesive system rather than as isolated components. Decisions were informed by visual calm, performance reliability, and operational efficiency — particularly important given the scale of the hotel and the ongoing demands of a high-use hospitality environment.

Marchese Partners project →

Shard 102 X Plan basins — integrated into a custom bench frame to support clean detailing and consistent joinery alignment across guest bathrooms (Azzurra Ceramica, Italy).

Specification & Collaboration

Studio Bagno worked closely with Marchese Partners throughout the specification process, supporting the selection and coordination of bathroom products aligned with both the architectural intent and the operational requirements of the hotel.

A key requirement was ensuring custom-designed basin bench frames integrated precisely with the selected basins. Studio Bagno supplied product samples early in the process, allowing the design team to finalise joinery dimensions and detailing with confidence and achieve a clean, consistent outcome across all guest rooms.

Customisation also played an important role in maintaining visual restraint. Slim actuator plates were specified in a custom grey soft-touch finish, closely colour-matched to the surrounding wall tiles. This allowed the plates to visually recede into the tile composition, reducing contrast and supporting a calm, integrated bathroom environment.

Guest room planning — a warm, resolved interior language carries through to the bathroom zone, reinforcing consistency across the guest experience.

From an operational perspective, water efficiency was a priority for the hotel operator. Oli 74 Mechanical In-Wall Cisterns were selected for their reliable performance and precise delivery of full and half flush volumes, helping minimise water wastage while reducing long-term maintenance and running cost considerations.

Across the project, Studio Bagno’s role was to support specification clarity — ensuring products met design intent, performed consistently at scale, and contributed to a cohesive bathroom solution suited to a contemporary hospitality setting.

Manhattan Rimless Wall Faced Pan — paired with a colour-matched slim actuator plate and supported by OLI 74 in-wall cisterns, specified for water efficiency, reliable performance, and reduced long-term maintenance (OLI, Portugal).

Interior palette — warm textiles and soft colour accents reinforce a relaxed, homely guest experience across the room and bathroom suite.

The Architect

Encore by Mingara was designed by Marchese Partners, an internationally recognised architecture and interior design practice with over three decades of experience delivering large-scale lifestyle, hospitality, residential, and mixed-use projects across Australia and internationally.

Across the hotel, the design approach prioritised clarity, consistency, and long-term performance — particularly within the bathrooms, where ceramic elements were resolved as part of a cohesive system rather than individual components. This disciplined approach supports visual calm, durability, and confidence at hospitality scale.

Marchese Partners →

“From the outset, the brief was to create hotel rooms that felt resolved and comfortable, with a design language that would age well. This meant prioritising clarity of form, durable materials, and a level of restraint appropriate to long-term hospitality use.”

Marchese Partners
